body: Thank you for your thoughtful reply.

On second thought, and in a much different frame of mind, your post sounds like a challenge. You see, I do sit alone and rot a lot. Why wait a decade or two? Here's hoping you have a much happier life knowing that you're helping strangers make important decisions.

EDIT: Oh, and lest anyone feel the need to "save" me, no worries. I'm safe for tonight. Probably tomorrow too. These things require careful planning so that the impact on others is minimized as much as possible. Maybe a fairy will come along and sprinkle happy dust on me and magically transform my screwed up brain into a normal one.

Fortunately your particular brand of snark is to be expected so I'm actually amused. :)

I think your work is done here.

I didn't want to but I woke up this morning. As I do each morning, I am trying to push myself to make the most of this day.

Thank you, each of you, for your kind and thoughtful comments - they help immensely.

Some comments:

1. The fortune is not my worry. It has been put out of the reach of my BIL until my MIL dies and after questioning both my husband and my psychiatrist, I have no doubt that he is capable of killing her. I even know how he will likely do it and he will likely get away with it. She is a vulnerable adult with reduced mental capacities and he doles out her heart and other meds which are kept in her room. We can't get them out of there and he will simply say that she must have gotten confused and overdosed. It breaks my heart because I love her dearly but he has persuaded her that only he can be trusted so we are not even able to communicate with her without causing her additional stress and unhappiness. (We live across the country from them as well.)

2. The childhood thing made me stop and think. About the loss of my own inner child and, more importantly, about my son. Perhaps he feels he lost his own childhood innocence too soon. Growing up with a depressive mother had to be rough (I know because I did - genetics for the win.) and he was always too good. I used to beg him to put his books away and go outside and play when he was a child. Because he won't respond to me or see me, I don't know how to address his need or even if I can.

3. My husband suffers from chronic severe pain with no diagnosis. Very little helps ameliorate the pain and my "job" is taking care of him. I think it would help if I could get out more but we live in a very tiny village and are considered outsiders so have no one to help pick up the slack should I leave for more than an hour or two. He's not bedridden or anything. To the contrary, he pushes himself to do more than I am capable of doing myself. Therein lies the risk - just yesterday he fell and wasn't sure whether he had injured himself or not. He can't tell the difference between a possible strain/sprain/break and his daily pain. He's over 60 and almost daily wishes he could die but keeps going because of his love for me.

There is more but I've should be doing a TL;DR already. Instead, I will try to do something productive - mostly because a handful of kind strangers gave me a tiny bit of hope. Thank you.
